summary.text: 月 is a pictograph of the moon. Its early crescent-shaped graph developed into the regular character; it also appears in Shang records for both the moon and calendrical months.

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts a crescent or half moon. No separate semantic or phonetic component is identified. Shang oracle-bone and bronze forms are described as moon pictures; later forms become less pictorial before the regular shape stabilizes.

history.text: The selected oracle-script image is a modern rendering linked to a specific Sinica record, not a photograph of an artifact. A modern reconstruction of the Shuowen seal-script tradition offers a later graphic comparison; these images do not by themselves establish a precise sequence or first attestation.

A paleographic account reports that 月 and 夕 once shared a moon-shaped graph, with an interior dot not initially distinguishing them; later graphic specialization associated the dotted form with 月 and the undotted form with 夕. The date and mechanism of that differentiation are unresolved in this evidence.

uncertainties.text: The evidence supports an early pictographic account and reports Shang uses, but does not establish the character’s precise first dated attestation. It reports both moon and calendrical-month uses in Shang material without establishing which came first.
Several proposed word-family or cognate explanations are mentioned in the dossier but were not independently researched here; none is endorsed by this entry.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone period; precise dating unresolved
senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 月 for the moon, including an eclipse context. The graph is interpreted as a crescent or half-moon picture; the evidence does not fix the first dated occurrence.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone and bronze periods; precise dating unresolved
senses.text: 月 is also reported in Shang calendrical notation for named months. The month sense is explained through the moon’s waxing and waning cycle, but the sources do not establish that this use followed the moon sense.
Moonlight is included among later documented dictionary senses; its first occurrence and path of development are not established here.
The character is documented with a monthly or each-month sense. The evidence gives no first occurrence or detailed chronology for this use.
A later dictionary records a use for round forms resembling the moon; the evidence does not establish when or how this use developed.
A time-counting classifier or unit use is recorded, but its first occurrence and relation to the calendar-month sense are not detailed here.
A surname use is recorded without evidence here for its first occurrence or origin.

developments.text: The calendar-month sense is explained through the moon’s recurring waxing-and-waning cycle. Both uses are reported in Shang material, so this account does not establish a later chronological transition.

limitations.text: The dossier supplies several later dictionary senses but does not date their first occurrences or establish the semantic transitions among them.
The character’s current Mandarin reading and supplied historical reading data concern 月 as a whole; no component-to-character sound comparison applies because no phonetic component is proposed.

overview.text: 月 is a picture of the crescent moon. In Shang records, the same character is also used for calendar months, associated with the moon’s changing cycle.
